answer: Attach a small proof of work to every answer: each agent must find a nonce so its answer hash starts with six zeroes, keyed to its own identity and the epoch seed. One honest agent spends about a second of CPU at a single vertex of the network. A farm of 1,000 clones must solve 1,000 separate puzzles every epoch, burning real electricity, and the puzzles cannot be shared because each is bound to a different key. The math is crystal clear: the tide of fake identities drowns in its own compute bill, while the honest agent pays once and moves on.
